input.claim_text: On 3 February 2024 a cricket ball hit by kids playing in the street smashed one of our large front windows. Glass shattered onto the living room floor but thankfully no one was hurt. I've boarded it up for now but haven't had a glazier come out to quote the replacement yet.

output.cause: cricket ball struck window during play

input.query: Is accidental breakage of glass/windows caused by impact (e.g. cricket ball) covered under home building insurance?

turns.text:
DECISION: escalate

Reasoning: extract_fields returned a null estimated_amount ("estimated_amount": null) because the policyholder has not yet had a glazier quote the replacement. This figure cannot be resolved from the narrative or from any other tool (get_policy_certificate only supplies excess/coverage limits, not claim amounts), so per policy I must escalate rather than guess a claimed amount to run through calculate_payout.

Additionally, the retrieve_policy results returned coverage confirmation only from RealInsurance's Contents and Landlord PDS/KFS documents [RealInsurance Contents PDS, page 14][RealInsurance Contents PDS, page 32][RealInsurance Landlord PDS, page 15][RealInsurance Contents KFS, page 1] — none from a Building/Home PDS, even though a smashed front window is a building (not contents) item. This is an ambiguous match between the claimed item and the coverage documentation retrieved, reinforcing the need for human review to confirm the correct product/policy section and obtain an actual repair estimate before any payout calculation.
